# --template-pattern narrows which templates are mutated; --run narrows
# which tests each mutant is run against. Both take regular expressions.
#
# The first run mutates only alpha and runs only TestAlpha, which renders
# alpha and compares the whole string, so the mutant is caught.
#
# The second run mutates only beta but still runs only TestAlpha. Nothing
# that executes is looking at beta, so the mutant survives. Narrowing --run
# narrows what can catch a mutant, which is what makes a miss reported
# under --run a statement about that subset and not about the whole suite.

muxt test-template-mutations --template-pattern '^alpha$' --run TestAlpha
cmp stdout want-alpha.txt

muxt test-template-mutations --template-pattern '^beta$' --run TestAlpha
cmp stdout want-beta.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "alpha"}}A{{.Name}}{{end}}
{{define "beta"}}B{{.Name}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Data struct {
	Name string
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func render(t *testing.T, name string) string {
	t.Helper()
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := templates.ExecuteTemplate(&buf, name, Data{Name: "x"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return buf.String()
}

func TestAlpha(t *testing.T) {
	if got, want := render(t, "alpha"), "Ax"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("alpha = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestBeta(t *testing.T) {
	if got, want := render(t, "beta"), "Bx"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("beta = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want-alpha.txt --
baseline ok
KILL templates.gohtml:1:20 "alpha" action-empty
1 mutant, 1 killed, 0 missed
-- want-beta.txt --
baseline ok
MISS templates.gohtml:2:19 "beta" action-empty
1 mutant, 0 killed, 1 missed
